Every call of this function made during the run counts as one invocation (all invocations of all test methods are pooled; their order does not matter for the answer).

Inside this function there is an outer `for` loop whose header is on line 219 (`for trial_numbers, values_info, best_values_info in info_list:`). One OUTER ITERATION is one execution of that loop's body first line (line 220), counted across all invocations. Inside the `if values_info.stds is None:` branch of the outer body there are two nested `for` loops: the loop with header on line 231 (body line 232) and the loop with header on line 234 (body line 235). (Line numbers are absolute, 1-based line numbers of `optuna/visualization/_optimization_history.py` as it exists in the repository.)

For each outer iteration, define its INNER ITERATION COUNT as the number of times line 232 executes plus the number of times line 235 executes during that outer iteration (i.e. the total number of iterations of both nested loops combined within that one outer iteration; an inner iteration = one execution of the nested loop body's first line). List comprehensions are not loops for this purpose and are not counted.

Consider only those outer iterations that take the `values_info.stds is None` branch (the condition on line 223 is true); outer iterations taking the `else` branch are ignored entirely. An outer iteration in which the branch is taken but neither nested loop iterates has inner iteration count 0 and IS included.

Report, over all those outer iterations across all invocations in all test methods:
- `max_iterations`: the largest inner iteration count (a JSON integer);
- `min_iterations`: the smallest inner iteration count (a JSON integer).

Answer as a JSON object with exactly the keys `max_iterations` and `min_iterations`.
